This is a suit filed by the plaintiff for declaration that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit schedule property and for direction to defendants No.1 to quit and deliver or restore the vacant possession of the suit property to plaintiff and for mesne profit at the rate of 20,000/- p.m. from 30.11.2012 till date of restoration of possession with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
2.

The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under:-
(a) The plaintiff is a member of defendant No.2 society i.e., M/s. Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society.

It had allotted and registered site No. 785 measuring East to west 70 feet and North to south 50 feet carved out in land bearing Sy.No. 101, 103, 104, 105 and 106 in 4 th phase of Girinagar, Bengaluru -85 of Hosakerehalli village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.

There were numerous litigations pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and various other courts in Bengaluru between the members of the society and defendant No.2 society, as there were some allegations against the society about illegality in allotment of sites, seniority and genuinity of members and also dispute between the society and land owners whose lands were acquired by the BDA.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to resolve the dispute passed a common order dtd: 16.11.2010 in the W.P. No. 6945/2008 and connected matters and gave guidelines to be followed by the society and the BDA, in allotment of sites to its members.

As per the directions of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the lands acquired by the BDA in Dr Belagavi C S vs Kamala N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19121792/
2 Sy.No.s.16,17,18 and 19 of Gerahalli village and 101,103/1,103/2,104/1,104/2,105,106 of Hosakere halli village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk totally measuring 80 acres 13 guntas executed sale deed in favour of the defendant No.2 society vide sale deed dtd: 18.6.2012.

sentences.text: Subsequently, rectification deed came to be executed by the BDA in favour of the society on 22.6.2012 rectifying the extent as 79 acres 00.75 guntas instead of 80 acres 13 guntas.
The BDA issued possession certificate and handed over the possession of the property to an extent of 79 acres 00.75 guntas vide possession certificate dtd: 23.6.2012.
Subsequently, defendant No.2 society prepared a new layout plan by forming various sites in the lands given to it and the BDA has approved the layout plan on 14.9.2012.

As per the directions of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No.6945/2008 and other connected matter, defendant No.2 society by way of paper publication called upon the members to produce documents to prepare a list of seniority,
genuineness and eligibility of members of society for allotment of sites.

Subsequent to the above said publication, plaintiff approached the society along with his previous sale deed dtd:
28.3.1994 executed by defendant No.2 and other documents.
The defendant No.2 society prepared a seniority, genuinity and eligibility members list who were to be allotted sites as per the directions of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The seniority list was published in local daily newspapers and it was made available to its members.

Defendant No.2 society after going through the sale deed and other documents produced by the plaintiff, satisfied with seniority and eligibility of the plaintiff for allotment of sites in the new layout formed by defendant No.2 society issued fresh allotment letter dtd 19.1.2012 confirming that earlier site bearing No.785 to be replaced with new site No. 3387 in 4th phase of VHBCS layout, Girinagar,
Bengaluru as per BDA approved layout plan dtd:14.9.2012.
Subsequently, defendant No.2 society executed registered supplemental deed with respect of site No.3387 in favour of the plaintiff.
The said site No. 3387 is referred as suit property.
After execution of registered supplemental deed the society issued possession certificate dtd: 5.9.2013 in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit property.
In all revenue records site shown as No.3387 not a site No. 785.
(b) The BDA issued show-cause notice to defendant No.1 calling upon her to vacate and hand over possession of the suit property to plaintiff.
But the defendant has not vacated the same.

Though defendant No.2 society through paper publication called upon the members to produce all other documents pertaining to seniority and eligibility of its members for allotment of sites in new layout plan, defendant No.1 has not approached the society for allotment of site in her favour and to prove her eligibility and seniority for allotment of site.
On the other hand, the defendant No.1 is illegally in possession of the site.
The defendant No.1 having failed to prove her eligibility and seniority for allotment of site has no right, interest over the suit property.
The defendant No.1 is in illegal possession and occupation of the suit property.
Hence, this suit.
3. (a) The defendants No.1 has appeared and filed written statement.
It is contended that plaintiff has suppressed the material facts and filed this suit.

The ancestors/family members of defendant No.1 were the owners of land bearing Sy.No.106 and other survey numbers of Hosakerehalli village,

sentences.text:
The family members of defendant No.1 acquired a portion of land in Sy.No.106 along with other lands by way of grant made by the Land Tribunal in No.
1062/74-75 and No.16,17,18 and 19/78-79.

The defendant No.2 society having interested in developing a residential layout in Sy.No.106 and other adjacent lands bearing No.101, 103, 104 and 105 for the purpose of formation of residential layout known as Vishvabharathi Housing Complex layout, 4th phase for the benefit of its members, approached the family members of defendant No.1 and another for possession of lands, consequent to the agreement entered into between the society and the family members of defendant No.1 and started layout work.
Defendant No.2 society formed layout only on the basis of the rights acquired from the ancestors of defendant No.1 and others who owned the lands.
Defendant No.2 society specifically assured the land owners that the society was allotted sites to the family members of land owners.

The defendant No.1 and other members of family of the land owners became the members of defendant No.2 society in terms of aforesaid understanding between them and the society, the defendant No.2 society agreed to allot sites to the family members of defendant No.1.

Accordingly, society allotted site No. 634 in the layout known as Vishwabhrathi Housing Complex layout, 4th phase, Girinagar, Bengaluru formed in Sy.No.101,103,104,105 and 106 of Hosakerehalli village and site No. 634 measuring East to west 50 feet and North to South 30 feet in total 1500 sq. feet, which is herein after referred as written statement schedule property.
The written statement schedule property allotted to defendant No.1 and she was put in possession of said site through a registered sale deed dtd:19.9.2003 executed by defendant No.2 society.
Possession certificate issued on 19.9.2003, since from the said date defendant No.1 is in possession of written statement schedule property.
Neither defendant No.1 nor any of her ancestors/ family members have received compensation or cost for the lands.
The society conveyed written statement schedule property in lieu of consideration payable by the society for the lands owned by the family members of defendant No.1.
The defendant No.1 being a senior member of defendant No.2 society and being entitled to site in terms of assurance to allot and convey site.
The defendant No.1 has constructed RCC building in it and presently she was let out to a tenant.
She has also obtained power connection and paying electricity bills in respect of the suit property.
Defendant No.2 cannot dispute that the agreement entered with family members of defendant No.1 and other land owners.

Defendant No.2 society which could not establish its challenge to acquisition proceedings initiated by BDA sought for bulk allotment of above said lands from BDA as a means to regularizing allotment of sites and transfer of absolute title to such members.
The bulk allotment of above lands by BDA and other proceedings were subject matter of writ petitions before the Hon'ble High Court and those writ petitions were disposed on 16.11.2010.

Writ petitions in No.18496/2007- connected matters, the Hon'ble High Court by order dtd:
16.11.2010 issued directions to defendant No.2 society to determine seniority and genuineness list of its members.

As per the above directions issued in the Hon'ble High Court, defendant No.2 society or any person claiming under the society cannot disturb the possession of the defendant No.1 with written statement schedule property.
Society has not included the name of defendant No.1 in the list of seniority/genuineness of the members of society.
In response to the public notice caused by society, the defendant No.1 along with her family members submitted representations along with necessary documents to defendant No.2 society on 9.9.2011.

sentences.text: The defendant No.2 society bypassed defendant No.1 and other senior members and tried to forcibly take possession of defendant No.1 property.
Therefore, defendant No.1 along with her brother filed civil suit in O.S.No.5858/2010 on the file of this court vide judgment and decree dtd: 7.10.2015.
The suit was decreed and defendant No.2 society was restrained from interfering with possession of defendant No.1.
Meanwhile the plaintiff tried to interfere with the possession of defendant No.1, on the basis of the supplemental deed allegedly executed by defendant No.2 society.
The defendant No.1 considering the filing of suit in O.S.No.3376/2014 before this court for the relief of permanent injunction against the plaintiff, the suit was decreed on 14.3.2023.
The written statement schedule property was allotted to defendant No.2, in lieu of consideration amount paid to the society.

The society had formed layout on the above mentioned lands only on the basis of rights acquired from the ancestors of defendant No.1 and allotted written statement schedule property in favour of defendant No.1.
Neither defendant No.2 society nor any person claiming under society can challenge the sale deed executed in favour of defendant No.1.

(b) The defendant No.2 society has lost right over the site No.634, after execution of the sale deed dtd: 19.9.2003 in favour of the defendant No.1 and therefore the Society had no subsisting right to allot or execute any document in respect of written statement schedule property either in favour of plaintiff or any other person.

The plaintiff, who is claiming under a document executed in his favour in the year 2012, cannot make any claim over the written statement schedule property, which is absolutely owned by the first defendant.

(c) The plaintiff who is claiming right, title and interest to the property bearing old site No.785(
which is situated far away from the first defendant's property in site No. 634 as per original/
previous layout plan) under the purported sale deed executed by 2nd defendant society, and further in collusion with the society has obtained supplemental deed, mischievously describing the first defendant's property( written statement schedule property) as site No.3387 with an intention to grab first defendant's valuable property.

Mere comparison of old layout plan and the new layout plan produced by the plaintiff clearly establish that the measurements, boundaries and the location of site No. 634 in the old plan and the site No.3387 in he new plan are different and do not refer to the same property.

The plaintiff cannot assert any right over the written statement schedule property, which is situated far away from site No.785, in the absence of any material to establish that property claimed by the plaintiff (site No.785) and the property owned by first defendant (site No.634) is one and the same.

(d) In the supplemental deed and the possession certificate it is clearly mentioned that 'the second party/plaintiff undertaken to take physical possession of the schedule property after the BDA evicts unauthorized occupants and hand over the same too the society as per the direction of the Hon'ble Dr Belagavi C S vs Kamala N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19121792/

It is clear from the aforesaid recital that the plaintiff is entitled to seek possession from the society, only after the sale deed/allotment in favour of the occupant/ first defendant is cancelled by the competent court and only after the BDA evicts the occupant and hand over possession of the same to the society.

The plaintiff cannot seek recovery of possession of purported site No.3387 or make any claim over written statement schedule property,
which is absolutely owned by first defendant in view of the specific recitals in his own documents.

(e) The Bangalore Development Authority, in view of the directions issued by the Hon'ble High Court, has issued notice to the first defendant and similarly placed persons, calling upon them to produce the documents on which basis the first defendant and similarly placed persons are in possession of their respective properties.

The first defendant appeared before the BDA and submitted her reply and the documents to establish her title and possession over site No.
634(written statement schedule property).

The BDA after verification of the records, filed objections in the W.P.NO.6945/2008 and connected matters, in response to the IA filed by the Society for implementation of the orders, specifically stating that the Society having allotted the sites and registered sale deeds for valuable consideration, is not justified in alleging that the occupants of the sites being trespassers.
The application filed by the society against the BDA in WP No. 6945/2008 and connected matters came to be rejected vide order dtd: 6.9.2018.

(e) The plaintiff who is aware of the first defendant's absolute ownership and possession over the written statement schedule property, has filed the above suit colluding with the Society, with an intention to grab the first defendant's property in site No. 634 (written statement schedule property)
(f) The first defendant is in possession and enjoyment of the written statement schedule property as the absolute owner.
Admittedly the 2nd defendant Society has not filed any suit or other proceedings for cancellation of the sale deed in favour of the first defendant in respect of written statement schedule property.
The first defendant is in possession and enjoyment of the from past 20 years and any claim for recovery of possession is barred by law of limitation.
There is no cause of action for the above suit and the cause of action pleaded is neither true or correct.
The suit is not properly valued and the court fee paid by the plaintiff is not sufficient.
The above suit is also bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following issues have been framed :-
1.
Whether the plaintiff proves that he is the absolute owner of the suit property having been allotted the same to him by defendant No.2 Society ?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendant No.1 is in illegal possession and occupation of the suit property ?

3. Whether the defendant No.1 proves that the written statement schedule property has been allotted to her by defendant No.2 society and she has been put in possession of the property from the date of issuance of possession certificate dtd: 19.9.2003?

11. The plaintiff has been examined as PW-1 and in his cross-examination he has stated that he is a member of defendant No.2 society since 1994.

15. In the present case, the plaintiff has contended that defendant No.1 is in illegal possession and occupation of the suit property belonging to the plaintiff.
In other words plaintiff is claiming that defendant is in illegal possession of the suit property.
Defendant No.1 is claiming that she is in possession of site No. 634, but the plaintiff is claiming that it is the suit property.
16. The defendant No.1 is not a party to the writ petitions upon which Ex.D-5 order has been passed.

Therefore, as per para No.44 (l) and (m), the society or BDA has to take appropriate proceedings against defendant No.1 who is admittedly in possession of suit property, which defendant no.1 claims to be site No.634, for cancellation of allotment of site to defendant No.1 and the sale deed executed in her name and also to recover possession from her.
But neither defendant No.2 nor BDA has taken any such steps as stated in para 44 (l) and (m) of the said order.
Therefore, status-quo shall be continued in respect of the property in possession of the plaintiff.
17. Ex.P-3 is the supplemental deed of plaintiff.
Already the relevant contents of said deed has been extracted in this Judgment.

The recitals in the supplemental deed shows that the plaintiff is not in immediate physical possession of the property and though the society has expressed its inability to execute any document in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff insisted for execution of necessary documents to vest title in him in furtherance of sale deed dtd: 28.03.1994/02.04.1994 and as per allotment letter dtd: 19.11.2012.

Further, it is stated that plaintiff has accepted the allotment letter with full knowledge that schedule property is in possession of unauthorized occupant and undertaken to take possession of schedule property after BDA evicts unauthorized occupant.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the sale deed executed in favour of defendant No.1 in respect of site No.634 has not been canceled and possession has not been recovered.
Under such circumstances, as per order or Hon'ble High Court as per Ex.D.5, it cannot be said that title has been passed to plaintiff on the basis of Ex.P-3 supplemental deed.

When the defendant No.2 society and BDA has not complied with para 44 (l) & (m) of writ petition order as per Ex.D-5, it can be said that present suit filed by the plaintiff is premature one and the Ex.P-3 supplemental deed executed by defendant No.2 in favour of the plaintiff will not give any right, title or interest over the suit property to the plaintiff, when the plaintiff is claiming the property in respect of which sale deed and possession letter has been issued in favour of the defandant no.1.

Considering the above circumstances, I am of the opinion that the plaintiff has failed to prove his title over the suit property and defendant No.1 is in illegal possession and occupation of the suit property.

When the conditions stated in para 44 (l) of writ petition order has not been complied and possession of the property from defendant No.1 has not been taken back, in view of the sale deed and the possession certificate issued in favour of defendant No.1, prima-facie it appears that written statement schedule property has been allotted to defendant No.1.
Accordingly, I answer Issues No.1 and 2 in the Negative and Issue No.3 in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.4:-
The documents in favour of defendant No.1 show that she is in possession of the suit property since from the year 2003.
Present suit has been filed in the year 2020 which is after 12 years from the date of possession letter issued in favour of defendant No.1.
However, the plaintiff is claiming right on the basis of Ex.P-3 supplemental deed and Ex.P-2 possession certificate, which is of the year 2012.
If the contention of the plaintiff is accepted that the right accrued to him on the basis of those documents, it cannot be said that the suit is barred by limitation.
The suit has been filed within 8 years.
Therefore, I answer Issue No.4 in the Negative.
19. Issue No.5:-
In view of the above discussion, the plaintiff is not entitled for the reliefs claimed in the suit.
Hence, I answer Issue No.5 in the Negative.
20. Issue No.6 :- In view of above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER The suit of the plaintiff is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw decree accordingly.
